title: The isolate, not the library
impact: Measurement + performance: rejected, and it closes a family that has eaten nine experiments. One row in the public release suite has resqlite losing to a peer -- `Single Inserts (100 sequential)` at 15.8 us per write against raw `sqlite3`'s 9.3 us on the same schema, journal mode and `synchronous` setting -- and exps 151, 170, 171, 182, 197, 214, 215, 257 and 271 each proposed a mechanism for that 6.4 us without first measuring where it goes. Three instruments, all AOT and lane-alternating in one process: eleven Stopwatch marks in the shipping path on both sides of the writer boundary, an `inline` reference running the identical `executeWrite` on the calling isolate, and -- the piece the previous nine did not have -- a `floor` lane that runs the same insert through a hand-rolled isolate writer with none of resqlite's machinery, so the isolate architecture can be priced on its own instead of being charged to the library. `db.execute` is 13.90 us, the floor is 12.92 us, inline is 7.61 us: 5.30 us of the 6.28 us hop is the isolate boundary and 0.98 us is everything resqlite does. The in-situ decomposition agrees independently at 1.21 us, spread over five items whose largest is 0.348 us -- 2.5% of a write. The boundary is not the object-graph copy: the same message costs 0.27 us to a port in the sending isolate, 0.45 us to an isolate draining a backlog and 0.74 us to a parked one, and the identical `executeWrite` costs 7.61 us inline against 9.38 us on a just-woken worker, so ~1.8 us of it is the woken side running cold. That refines claim 279.1's 1.46 us round trip, which was measured against an echo isolate that never goes cold. The candidate the decomposition named -- dropping the per-request reply `SendPort` from all eight writer request types, redundant since exp 159's persistent reply port -- was implemented and rejected: the `send` slice it targets reads 1.471-1.484 us against 1.469-1.521 us. Runtime reverted; prototype and probes at `archive/exp-284`; harness retained as `benchmark/experiments/write_hop_decomposition.dart`, whose `--part=floor` lane is the gate any future write-path candidate should be sized against.
